title: Asthma long-term management (adults and adolescents)
subject: respiratory
summary: Every adult or adolescent with asthma needs ICS-containing treatment. GINA 2026 prefers Track 1: as-needed low-dose ICS-formoterol (Steps 1 to 2), then ICS-formoterol maintenance and reliever therapy (Steps 3 to 5); step up only after checking technique and adherence, and step down after 3 months of good control.

sections.title: Confirm diagnosis and assess control
items: Document variable expiratory airflow limitation: bronchodilator responsiveness (FEV1 or FVC rise of 12% or more and 200 mL or more), excessive PEF variability or a positive challenge test. BTS/NICE/SIGN 2024: FeNO 50 ppb or more, or a raised blood eosinophil count, supports the diagnosis in adults.

Symptom control over the past 4 weeks: daytime symptoms more than twice a week, any night waking, SABA reliever more than twice a week, any activity limitation. None = well controlled, 1 to 2 = partly controlled, 3 to 4 = uncontrolled.

Exacerbation risk factors even with few symptoms: SABA overuse (3 or more 200-dose canisters a year; 1 or more a month is very high risk), no ICS or poor technique, FEV1 below 60% predicted, smoking, obesity, rhinosinusitis, GERD, food allergy, pregnancy, psychosocial problems, previous exacerbations.
Measure FEV1 at the start, after 3 to 6 months of ICS-containing treatment (personal best), then periodically.

sections.title: Track 1 (preferred): ICS-formoterol reliever
items: Starting step: symptoms less than 3 to 5 days a week with normal or mildly reduced lung function: AIR-only. Symptoms most days, night waking weekly or more, or low lung function: low-dose MART. Daily symptoms or weekly night waking with low lung function or a recent exacerbation: medium-dose MART.
Steps 1 to 2 (AIR-only): budesonide-formoterol 160/4.5 mcg delivered (200/6 mcg metered), 1 inhalation whenever needed for symptoms, before exercise or allergen exposure. No maintenance dose.

Step 3 (low-dose MART): 1 inhalation twice (or once) daily plus 1 inhalation as needed. Step 4 (medium-dose MART): 2 inhalations twice daily plus 1 as needed. High-dose ICS-formoterol is not used at Step 4.
Step 5: refer for phenotyping; consider add-on LAMA, a trial of high-dose maintenance ICS-formoterol, and biologic therapy (anti-IgE, anti-IL5/5R, anti-IL4R alpha, anti-TSLP).

Seek medical care the same day if more than 12 inhalations (maintenance plus reliever) are needed in 24 hours. Beclometasone-formoterol 100/6 mcg can be used for MART the same way. No separate SABA is needed.

Do not use budesonide-formoterol 400/12 mcg (320/9 delivered) or beclometasone-formoterol 200/6 mcg as a reliever, and do not use ICS-formoterol as a reliever alongside a different ICS-LABA maintenance inhaler.

sections.title: Track 2 (alternative): ICS-SABA or SABA reliever
items: Use when Track 1 is not possible, or when asthma is stable on current therapy with good adherence and no exacerbations. Before relying on a SABA reliever, check the patient will take maintenance ICS daily.

Step 1: as-needed low-dose ICS-SABA (budesonide-salbutamol 80/90 mcg delivered, 2 inhalations as needed; seek care if more than 12 inhalations in 24 hours), or low-dose ICS taken every time SABA is taken.
Step 2: daily low-dose ICS (budesonide 200 to 400 mcg/day, standard-particle beclometasone 200 to 500 mcg/day, or fluticasone propionate 100 to 250 mcg/day).

Step 3: low-dose ICS-LABA. Step 4: medium-dose ICS-LABA (e.g. budesonide above 400 to 800 mcg/day). Step 5: add-on LAMA (tiotropium or a triple inhaler), refer, consider high-dose ICS-LABA and biologics.
Reliever at every step: as-needed ICS-SABA, or SABA if ICS-SABA is unavailable. Never prescribe SABA without an ICS (BTS/NICE/SIGN 2024).

sections.title: Review, step up and step down
items: Review 1 to 3 months after starting or changing treatment, then every 3 to 12 months, and within 1 week of an exacerbation. Check symptoms, exacerbations, inhaler technique, adherence, side-effects and comorbidities every time.

Before any step-up confirm the symptoms are asthma and correct technique, adherence, smoking and exposures. Treat a sustained step-up as a 2 to 3 month trial; if no response, return to the previous step.
Short-term step-up for 1 to 2 weeks (viral infection, allergen season) can be patient-initiated through the written action plan.

Step down when well controlled with stable lung function for about 3 months: reduce ICS by 25 to 50% at 3-month intervals. MART: medium to low maintenance, then once-daily low-dose maintenance, then consider AIR-only. Never stop ICS completely.
Do not step down during a respiratory infection, while travelling, or in pregnancy. Stopping the LABA when reducing ICS-LABA can cause deterioration.

sections.title: Refer and add-on options
items: Refer for specialist advice after hospitalisation or repeated emergency visits, more than 1 to 2 exacerbations a year despite medium or high-dose ICS-LABA, diagnostic doubt, or suspected occupational asthma.
BTS/NICE/SIGN 2024: if uncontrolled on moderate-dose MART, check FeNO and blood eosinophils and refer if either is raised; if both are normal, consider an 8 to 12 week trial of an LTRA or LAMA.
Montelukast can cause serious behavioural and mood changes including suicidal ideation; discuss before prescribing.
Maintenance oral corticosteroids are a last resort: even 4 to 5 lifetime courses increase the risk of diabetes, osteoporosis, cataract and heart failure.

sections.title: Non-pharmacological care
items: Written asthma action plan for every patient, stating how to increase treatment and when to seek care.
Smoking and vaping cessation, avoidance of relevant allergen and occupational exposures, physical activity, and weight reduction if obese.
Vaccination as per national schedule (influenza, COVID-19, RSV where recommended).
Consider house dust mite SLIT for sensitised patients with not-well-controlled but stable asthma.

sections.title: Special situations
items: Pregnancy: continue ICS-containing treatment; poorly controlled asthma carries more risk to mother and fetus than asthma medicines. Avoid stepping down during pregnancy.
Asthma-COPD overlap: always include an ICS; never give LABA or LAMA without ICS to anyone with asthma features.
Budesonide-formoterol 200/6 mcg metered-dose inhalers correspond to the GINA 160/4.5 mcg delivered dose used for AIR and MART. Use a spacer with any pMDI.

sections.title: Pitfalls
items: SABA-only treatment, or a separate SABA prescribed alongside MART.
Switching between ICS products at 'equivalent' doses without review: dose tables do not imply potency equivalence.
Stepping up for poor technique, non-adherence or a non-asthma cause of breathlessness.
Not shaking a suspension pMDI immediately before each actuation, which gives unpredictable doses.

drugs.name: Budesonide-formoterol 160/4.5 mcg delivered (200/6 mcg metered)
drugs.dose: AIR-only: 1 inhalation as needed. MART Step 3: 1 inhalation twice (or once) daily plus 1 as needed. MART Steps 4 to 5: 2 inhalations twice daily plus 1 as needed
drugs.notes: Seek care if more than 12 total inhalations in 24 hours. Not the 400/12 mcg strength as reliever.

drugs.name: Beclometasone-formoterol 100/6 mcg
drugs.dose: MART: 1 inhalation twice daily (Step 3) or 2 inhalations twice daily (Steps 4 to 5), plus 1 inhalation as needed
drugs.notes: Maximum 12 inhalations in 24 hours; 200/6 mcg strength must not be used as reliever.

drugs.name: Budesonide-salbutamol 80/90 mcg delivered
drugs.notes: Track 2 reliever; seek same-day care if more than 12 inhalations (6 doses) in 24 hours. Not for MART.

drugs.name: Budesonide (ICS)
drugs.dose: Low 200 to 400 mcg/day; medium above 400 to 800 mcg/day; high above 800 mcg/day
drugs.notes: Adults and adolescents 12 years and older (GINA Box 4-2).

drugs.name: Fluticasone propionate (ICS)
drugs.dose: Low 100 to 250 mcg/day; medium above 250 to 500 mcg/day; high above 500 mcg/day
drugs.notes: Dose bands are not potency equivalents.

drugs.name: Beclometasone dipropionate, standard particle (ICS)
drugs.dose: Low 200 to 500 mcg/day; medium above 500 to 1000 mcg/day; high above 1000 mcg/day

drugs.name: Tiotropium (soft mist inhaler)
drugs.dose: 5 mcg (2 puffs of 2.5 mcg) once daily
drugs.notes: Step 5 add-on to medium or high-dose ICS-LABA.

drugs.name: Salbutamol
drugs.dose: 100 to 200 mcg (1 to 2 puffs) by pMDI as needed
drugs.notes: Track 2 reliever only when ICS-SABA unavailable; always with maintenance ICS.
